ai.title: Clarify terminal verification protocol in system prompt
ai.summary: System prompt section renamed from 'Verifying changes' to 'To complete a response, run commands to check for correctness'. Instruction now explicitly directs agent to check knowledge files for verification protocols before running terminal commands. Scope limited to backend/src/system-prompt.ts. Small change exception for confident single-line edits retained but moved inline.

eli5.text: Your AI helper now checks a guidebook before running its own tests to confirm changes are correct. Instead of deciding on its own whether to run verification commands, it first looks at the project's knowledge files to see exactly which commands (like tests or code checks) should be run, and runs all of them together. This change is already live today and only affects the AI's internal decision-making process, nothing visible to users has changed, but you might notice the AI takes a slightly more consistent approach to checking its work.

ai.title: Refine agent stop logic and continue tool payload
ai.summary: Updated `checkConversationProgress` in `backend/src/conversation-progress.ts` to require explicit confirmation of full user request satisfaction rather than minimal completion. The function now returns an object containing `shouldStop` and a `response` string detailing remaining tasks. In `backend/src/main-prompt.ts`, stop marker handling was restructured to pass the progress check response to the `continue` tool call. `npm-app/src/tool-handlers.ts` was modified to consume this `input.response` payload, replacing the static 'Please continue.' string.

eli5.text: When the assistant decides it has done enough to help you, it used to settle for doing just barely enough. Now it must confirm it has fully addressed your whole request before stopping, and when it does keep going, it carries a short status note about what’s still left to do instead of the fixed line 'Please continue.' This affects how the assistant wraps up multi-step tasks. Live today, so you may notice the assistant works a bit longer before deciding it’s truly finished.

ai.title: Report usage to Stripe meter events
ai.summary: Message costs reported to Stripe billing meter events asynchronously after DB save in `backend/src/billing/message-cost-tracker.ts`. `stripe.billing.meterEvents.create` called with `event_name: 'credits'`, `stripe_customer_id`, and `value` from `creditsUsed`. Only for authenticated users with active subscriptions and non-zero credits. `common/src/util/string.ts` `pluralize` updated to include count in output string.

ai.title: System prompt clarifies full-file overwrite for editfile
ai.summary: The system prompt in `backend/src/system-prompt.ts` now explicitly instructs the agent to write the entire file content when overwriting, forbidding truncation with placeholder comments. This change targets the `edit_file` block mechanism to prevent incomplete file rewrites. The update is internal to the backend prompt logic.

eli5.text: Your digital helper now writes out complete file contents when replacing an existing file, rather than leaving parts blank with placeholder comments. If you ever inspect a file after an edit, you won’t see incomplete sections marked with notes like "rest stays the same." This keeps the helper from accidentally cutting off important code when it updates files.

ai.title: Add break to SKIPPEDTERMINALCOMMANDS
ai.summary: Added 'break' to SKIPPED_TERMINAL_COMMANDS in common/src/constants.ts. Prevents terminal handling for this command. Scope limited to shared core constants. Internal refactor.

eli5.text: The assistant now treats 'break' as a command to leave alone, so it won't try to manage the terminal when that word is used. This only affects the shared list of commands the system skips, and it's already active today.

ai.title: Add createdat to fingerprint table
ai.summary: Added `created_at` column to `fingerprint` table in `common/src/db/schema.ts` via migration `0008_puzzling_carnage.sql`. Column is `timestamp`, `NOT NULL`, defaults to `now()`. Updates Drizzle journal and snapshot metadata. No user-facing behavior change; internal DB schema only.

eli5.text: Each fingerprint record in the database now stores the moment it was created, automatically set when the record is added. You won't see this date anywhere in the app, because it's behind-the-scenes data that only the system uses for tracking. The column is already live, but nothing in the current app actually reads it yet, so it does nothing until a future feature starts using it.
